subject: vectorizing lower/upper bounds for constrained variables

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: vectorizing lower/upper bounds for constrained variables
parts:
On Mar 4, 2014, at 8:39 PM, Ben Goodrich <goodri...@gmail.com> wrote:

> The limitation that lower and upper bounds can only be scalars is pretty limiting in my opinion.
>

This is a separate issue from the function language, so I dropped
it in a new thread.

I agree that it's limiting.

It's a bit tricky to extend the language, but it'd be a great
project.

The main issue is how to test that the lower/upper bounds conform
to the dimensions of the variable.

Case 1.

real<lower=L,upper=U> a[N];

If L and U are either scalars or 1D arrays of size N,
it's easy. Should we also allow row vectors or column vectors?

Case 2.

real<lower=L,upper=U> b[M,N];

Here I think we'd want L and U to be 2D arrays (maybe matrices,
arrays of vectors, etc.?)

Case 3.

vector<lower=L,upper=U>[N] x;

Again, this is easy if L or U are scalars or 1D vectors of size
N (or arrays? or row vectors?).

Case 4.

vector<lower=L,upper=U>[N] x[M];

Here I think it makes sense to take L to be scalars or 1D
vectors (arrays/row vectors) of size N. But should we also
allow matrices (arrays) of size M x N? Or mixtures of vectors
and matrices?

- Bob

parts:
I don’t know — different constraints imply fundamentally
different types to me, and it makes much less sense to have
a vector/matrix/etc of mixed types as opposed to the same type.

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: vectorizing lower/upper bounds for constrained variables
parts:
We have the same sort of issue with the never-implemented syntax

matrix ~ distribution(vector, scalar);

as in

Y ~ normal(mu_vec, sigma);

so whatever we decide is supported for that, we might as do the same thing the bounds on declared parameters.

I think my position was "all pieces must match each other exactly (in type and size), except that a scalar matches with anything". So, the above would actually be illegal unless the user broadcasted mu_vec into a matrix with the same dimensions as Y.

Ben
